headline: Dow down 1.1% as crude jumps 4% to $103; bitcoin flat near $81,200
summary: Oil is still setting the tone: U.S. crude is up about 4% to roughly $103.50 and Brent is near $116, its highest since March, keeping the Dow down 1.1% (about 590 points), the S&P 500 down 0.5% and the TSX down 0.3% as of 3:23 p.m. ET, while a chip rebound (AMD up 1.7%) keeps the Nasdaq's loss to 0.1%. Crypto is calm: bitcoin is flat at about $81,200 and ether is up 0.3% to about $2,390, with Fear & Greed at 50 (Neutral); AKEDO (+23%) and PEPE (+7%) lead the top 100 while Lighter (-9%), Worldcoin (-8%) and Aerodrome (-7%) lag, and the small data-network token Irys is trending after rising about six-fold in two days with no confirmed catalyst. The 10-year yield is near 5.0%, gold is down 1.2% to about $4,011, the VIX fear gauge is near 20, and the loonie is up to 71.4 U.S. cents ahead of Wednesday's Fed and Bank of Canada decisions.

crypto.label: Cautious
crypto.why: Bitcoin and ether are stuck in a tight range near the bottom of their monthly band, spot bitcoin ETFs just had their biggest daily outflow since June, and the Fear & Greed index has dropped from 68 to 50 in a day.

stocks.label: Mixed
stocks.why: Chip stocks are limiting the Nasdaq's losses, but crude near $103.50, a 10-year yield at 5%, a VIX near 20 and consumer sentiment near a record low (48.0) are dragging the Dow, banks and the TSX lower.

drivers.title: AI-spending doubts hit Big Tech and chips
drivers.detail: Meta closed down 7% Thursday despite beating forecasts as investors weighed its $135–$145 billion spending plan; AMD, Amazon, Nvidia and Broadcom fell 4–8%. Friday the selling has eased: AMD is up about 1.7% and the Nasdaq is only slightly lower, though Meta, Amazon and Alphabet are still slipping ahead of more Big Tech results next week.
drivers.assets: Nasdaq, chip stocks, Shopify, Celestica, bitcoin

drivers.title: Yields climb back to 5%
drivers.detail: After its biggest one-day drop in more than a year Thursday, the 10-year Treasury yield is back at about 5.0% as oil revives inflation worries; the University of Michigan survey shows year-ahead inflation expectations up to 4.7%. CME FedWatch data show only about an 8% chance of a Fed hike on Oct. 28, but roughly 84% odds of one by year-end.

drivers.title: U.S. crude near $103 on Gulf escalation
drivers.detail: U.S. crude is up about 4% to roughly $103.50 and Brent has climbed to about $116, its highest since March and up from under $97 at the start of October, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, Iranian threats against Gulf energy sites, and a U.S. envoy's warning that the Iran war could last another year. Higher oil feeds inflation fears days before the Fed and Bank of Canada meet, lifts Canadian producers and weighs on consumers and bonds.

drivers.title: SpaceX wireless report hits U.S. telecoms
drivers.detail: AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile slid after Bloomberg reported SpaceX wants access to about 80,000 U.S. cell sites and is talking with tower owners; Crown Castle jumped about 10% premarket. Verizon is a Dow member, and the telecom drop, together with American Express (down about 3%) and JPMorgan (down 1.7%), helps explain why the Dow, down about 1.1%, is the weakest U.S. index.

drivers.title: Bitcoin ETFs post biggest outflow since June
drivers.detail: Spot bitcoin ETFs (funds that hold real bitcoin) took in about $1.08 billion over the prior three days, then lost about $635 million on Thursday, the largest one-day outflow since June 25 per SoSoValue data, while ether funds have lost more than $1 billion this month. About $406 million of leveraged crypto bets were wiped out over 24 hours, per CoinGlass.

drivers.title: Bank of Canada rate hike now likely
drivers.detail: Swap markets price about 80% odds of a Bank of Canada hike to 2.50% on Oct. 28 after strong retail sales and Governor Macklem's warning on oil-driven inflation. The loonie is up about 0.3% to 71.4 U.S. cents, near a one-month high, while RBC and TD are both down about 0.3–0.4%.

crypto.name: Bitcoin
crypto.move: Flat (down 0.2%) over 24h and up 0.4% this week, at about $81,200 (down 3.4% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Bitcoin fell back below $82,000 Thursday as Meta's and Tesla's results revived doubts about AI spending, and it has traded in a range of under $1,000 since, near $81,000–$82,000, and it is drifting at the low end of that band this afternoon. Spot bitcoin ETFs (funds that hold real bitcoin) lost about $635 million Thursday, the most in a day since June, and oil's jump to a five-month high is adding to inflation and rate worries before the Fed meets.
crypto.meaning: Bitcoin is now trading closely with tech stocks, and it is sitting just above the $80,000 floor of the $80,000–$87,000 range it has held for a month. ETF buying helps, but it is below the pace that came with past strong rallies, and some traders warn that a clean break below about $80,000 could open a slide toward $75,000 or lower. CoinDesk notes it is still about 40% above its July 1 low of $57,850, which some analysts read as this cycle's bottom.

outlook.bullCase: Reclaiming $84,000–$85,000 with steady ETF inflows and a firmer Nasdaq could carry it to the top of the range near $87,000–$87,500; a break above that would be a bigger shift.
outlook.bearCase: A further slide in tech stocks, a hawkish Fed on Oct. 28, or higher oil could push it below the $80,000 floor, with some traders eyeing $75,000–$70,000 if that gives way.
outlook.watch: Whether the Nasdaq's rebound holds into the close, the $80,000 and $85,000 levels, whether Thursday's large ETF outflows continue, and the Fed decision on Oct. 28.

crypto.name: Ethereum
crypto.move: Up 0.3% over 24h, down 0.3% this week, at about $2,390 (down 10% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Ether has slipped just below the $2,400 level that had acted as support for about a week. Ether ETFs lost about $110 million Thursday and more than $1 billion in October, the worst month of the year for them, so big-investor demand keeps fading even when bitcoin holds steady.
crypto.meaning: Ether is lagging bitcoin because big investors keep pulling money from the ETFs. Until those flows turn, rallies may be harder to sustain.

outlook.bullCase: Holding above $2,400, ETF outflows stopping and a firm hold above $2,500 could open a move toward about $2,700, where October began.
outlook.bearCase: Staying below $2,400 with continued ETF outflows could send it toward the $2,300 area, and a broader risk-off turn could push it lower.
outlook.watch: Daily ether ETF flows, the $2,400 and $2,500 levels, the ETH/BTC ratio, and any new Glamsterdam upgrade timeline.

crypto.name: Pepe
crypto.move: Up 6.6% in 24h and 20% this week, at about $0.0000047 (up 8.5% over 30 days); trending on CoinGecko
crypto.why: PEPE, the largest frog-themed meme coin (a token with no product, driven by online hype), is the biggest gainer among large coins today. There is no official news behind it: on Oct. 21 it had the biggest jump in trading activity on South Korean exchanges relative to normal, and futures trading has been running at more than five times spot trading, with open interest (the value of open bets) near $270 million, per CoinMarketCap's summary of market data. Early Friday CoinDesk flagged it up about 13% as smaller coins bounced while bitcoin held steady.
crypto.meaning: Gains built on borrowed money and a burst of retail trading in one region can unwind fast if those bets are closed. PEPE is still far below its December 2024 record, and meme coins tend to swing much more than bitcoin in both directions.

outlook.bullCase: If meme-coin interest keeps building and bitcoin holds $80,000, PEPE could extend toward the $0.0000055–$0.000006 area.
outlook.bearCase: A wider crypto sell-off or a wave of liquidations (leveraged bets closed automatically) could erase the week's gain and send it back toward $0.0000041–$0.0000044.
outlook.watch: Futures open interest and funding rates, Korean exchange volume, and whether bitcoin holds $80,000.

crypto.name: Aerodrome Finance
crypto.move: Down 7.0% in 24h and 12% this week, at about $0.745 (up 12% over 30 days); trending on CoinGecko
crypto.why: Aerodrome, the biggest trading exchange on Coinbase's Base network, merged with its sister exchange Velodrome into a single platform called Aero, which went live on seven blockchains around Oct. 21–22. The token has fallen since in a classic 'sell the news' reaction: futures open interest (the value of open bets) dropped about 8% as traders cut leverage, and it broke below the $0.79–$0.80 support area that analysts had flagged.
crypto.meaning: The merger gives Aero a bigger footprint, but the market had priced it in, and old Velodrome holders received new AERO that some are selling. With the old support gone, swings are likely until the new token supply settles.

outlook.bullCase: Strong trading volume on the new multi-chain Aero and a quick reclaim of $0.79–$0.80 could carry it back toward $0.85–$0.90.
outlook.bearCase: Continued selling from converted Velodrome holders and a weak market could push it toward $0.65–$0.70.
outlook.watch: Daily trading volume and fees on Aero, whether it reclaims $0.80, and governance votes on emission (new token) rates.

crypto.name: AKEDO
crypto.move: Up 23% in 24h and 23.5% this week, at about $0.0384 (down 21% over 30 days)
crypto.why: AKEDO is a small AI-tools token that has just squeezed into CoinGecko's top 100. We could not find a clear news catalyst for the jump, which peaked overnight near $0.037 eased to about $0.035 and is now edging above that level near $0.038; it comes two days after a scheduled Oct. 21 unlock of tokens worth about $63 million (roughly 9% of its market value), and after weeks stuck in a $0.029–$0.037 range. Earlier community analysis found the top 100 wallets hold almost all of the supply, so a few holders can move the price sharply.
crypto.meaning: A double-digit jump on no identifiable news, in a token with extremely concentrated ownership, is the kind of move that can reverse just as quickly. The price is now testing just above the old $0.037 ceiling, and anyone holding it is exposed to large holders and fresh unlocked supply.

outlook.bullCase: Holding above the old $0.037 ceiling on steady volume would turn that level into support and could extend the move.
outlook.bearCase: Selling by large holders or recipients of the Oct. 21 unlock could send it back into the $0.029–$0.03 range or toward about $0.022, a level flagged as key support.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds above about $0.03, trading volume, large-wallet transfers to exchanges, and any official project news.

crypto.name: Ethena
crypto.move: Up 3.3% in 24h and 6.6% this week, at about $0.207 (down 1.1% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Ethena runs USDe, a synthetic dollar token that earns yield by pairing crypto holdings with offsetting futures bets. ENA has climbed for a third day since Oct. 21, as traders focus on the protocol's fees (it has generated more than $1 billion in total, per analyst Lark Davis), $1.3 billion of new deposits since August, and asset manager Janus Henderson's plan to use staked USDe for cash management. All remaining early-investor tokens unlocked on Oct. 5, so that supply overhang has passed.
crypto.meaning: The story is better fees and institutional use, but ENA's planned buybacks only switch on once USDe supply reaches $7.5 billion, well above the roughly $4.6 billion reported in August. ENA was rejected near $0.215 earlier this week, and after testing that ceiling again earlier today it has slipped back to about $0.207.

outlook.bullCase: A clean break above about $0.215 on rising USDe supply could open a move toward $0.24–$0.25.
outlook.bearCase: Another rejection at $0.215, or a wider altcoin sell-off, could send it back to the $0.18–$0.19 area where this week's move began.
outlook.watch: USDe circulating supply (the $7.5 billion buyback trigger), the $0.215 level, and large-holder sales; about 20% of supply sits with treasury firm StablecoinX under a separate lockup.

crypto.name: Lighter
crypto.move: Down 9.2% in 24h, up 6.7% this week, at about $3.26 (down 39% over 30 days)

outlook.bearCase: No confirmation, or more profit-taking after Wednesday's 20% jump, could send it back toward about $3.20 or below.

crypto.name: Monero
crypto.move: Down 2.5% in 24h but up 8.0% this week, at about $595 (up 8.6% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Monero, a privacy-focused coin that hides who sends what, has slipped from about $650 late Wednesday to near $595 and is down about 2.5% over the past day, though it is still up about 8% on the week. We found no project-specific news behind the pullback (the latest software release on Oct. 16 was routine maintenance), so it looks like the crowded leveraged trade unwinding as the wider market cooled. The run had started after veteran chart trader Peter Brandt called XMR his favourite large-cap setup, and futures trading had outpaced spot (actual coin) trading, with funding rates (the fee bullish leveraged traders pay to keep bets open) near 70% a year, per CoinDesk.
crypto.meaning: Rallies driven by borrowed money can reverse quickly if traders are forced to close positions (a liquidation). Monero is also still about 18% below its January record near $799, and an EU anti-money-laundering rule from July 2027 will bar regulated crypto firms from handling privacy coins, which limits where it can trade.

outlook.bullCase: Holding above the old $600 resistance could keep momentum going toward the $700 area and, beyond that, the January high near $799.
outlook.bearCase: A leverage flush could drag it back through $600 toward the $520–$560 zone where it bounced earlier this month.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds the $600 line, futures open interest and funding rates (falling funding would mean the leverage is clearing out), spot versus futures volume, and any exchange delisting news.

crypto.name: Zcash
crypto.move: Up 0.4% over 24h and 8.1% this week, at about $1,224 (down 18.6% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Traders had been positioning for the NU7 upgrade, which developers scheduled for about 7:50 p.m. ET on Nov. 5; it cuts block times from 75 to 25 seconds and sends 60% of fees to a reserve. Futures open interest (the value of open bets) had risen about 19–24% and two large traders reportedly opened about $37.6 million of 10x leveraged longs. Those leveraged bets have been unwinding: CoinDesk flagged ZEC among the coins where bullish traders were closing positions, and the price has dropped back to just above the $1,190–$1,230 support area, where it is holding today.
crypto.meaning: Much of this month's rally was driven by borrowed money, and today shows how fast that can reverse. Upgrade dates often bring 'buy the rumour, sell the news' behaviour, so swings both ways are likely into Nov. 5.

outlook.bullCase: Holding the $1,180–$1,200 area and renewed interest as the upgrade nears could bring it back to the $1,375 resistance and, beyond that, the September high near $1,700.
outlook.bearCase: Losing $1,180 would erase the October breakout and could send it toward about $1,000–$1,120, near its 50-day average.
outlook.watch: The $1,180 level, funding rates and open interest, ETF flows, and any upgrade delay.

crypto.name: Solana
crypto.move: Up 0.1% over 24h and 0.5% this week, at about $103.60 (down 9.1% over 30 days); trending on CoinGecko
crypto.why: Solana completed its Alpenglow upgrade, a major overhaul aimed at much faster transaction finality (the point at which a payment can't be reversed), according to CoinDesk. The price has moved with the market rather than rallying on the news, and it is roughly flat over the past day near $103.60.
crypto.meaning: A smooth Alpenglow launch is a meaningful technical milestone, but the market is treating it as already expected. The first days after a big upgrade are when problems usually show up, so stability matters more than headlines.

outlook.bullCase: A trouble-free upgrade and stronger crypto risk appetite could lift SOL back toward $115–$120.
outlook.bearCase: Any outage or bug after the upgrade, or a bitcoin break below $80,000, could push SOL under $100.
outlook.watch: Network stability after Alpenglow, bitcoin's $80,000–$85,000 range, and Solana ETF flows.

stocks.name: S&P 500
stocks.move: Down 0.5% at about 7,629 as of 3:23 p.m. ET; about 2.7% below its record near 7,845
stocks.why: Oil near $103 and yields back at 5% are weighing on the index, which pared an early 0.6% drop around midday but has slipped again this afternoon; about four in five S&P 500 stocks were lower in the morning, per AP. Banks, telecoms and consumer names lead the decline, and the University of Michigan's final October consumer sentiment reading slipped to 48.0, near a record low, with year-ahead inflation expectations at 4.7%.
stocks.meaning: The damage is concentrated in tech, which makes up a large share of the index, while other sectors are holding up better. Falling bond yields help a little, but a 10-year yield near 5% still makes stocks look expensive relative to bonds.

outlook.bullCase: Solid results from Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon next week, a calm Fed on Oct. 28 and yields easing further could carry it back toward the 7,845 record.
outlook.bearCase: A deeper tech sell-off, a hawkish Fed, or an oil spike above $115 could drag it below 7,600 toward the 7,500 area.
outlook.watch: Whether 7,600 holds into the close, oil prices, and the Fed decision on Oct. 28 followed by Microsoft and Alphabet earnings that evening.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.move: Down 0.5% to about $645.60 as of 3:23 p.m. ET, after Thursday's 7% drop; it touched $633 early
stocks.why: Third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, beating forecasts, and fourth-quarter guidance topped estimates, but the stock fell as investors focus on costs: Meta expects $135–$145 billion of capital spending, free cash flow was about -$2.1 billion this quarter, and a $9.9 billion legal charge cut reported profit. It also surprised Wall Street with a new non-voting Class C share, one for every share held starting in January 2027; JPMorgan's Doug Anmuth called the pending shares an overhang (a supply worry hanging over the price) and urged Meta to issue any new stock quickly. Meta's filing says the Class C dividend is expected to work like a two-for-one stock split for Class A holders.
stocks.meaning: The core ad business is growing fast, which supports the stock, but AI spending pushed free cash flow negative (about -$2.1 billion) this quarter. A separate $25 billion penalty imposed by a New Mexico judge in a privacy case is under appeal and adds legal uncertainty.

outlook.bullCase: At least 13 brokerages raised price targets after the results, per LSEG; if buyers return to the strong ad growth, it could recover toward the $700 level.
outlook.bearCase: Worry about open-ended AI spending, a share sale to fund it, or the $25 billion New Mexico penalty could push it below Thursday's low near $640 toward the $620–$630 area.
outlook.watch: Whether Thursday's low near $640 holds, any details on Class C share issuance, and Alphabet's and Microsoft's spending plans on Oct. 28.

outlook.bearCase: If the AI-spending worry deepens, it could slide toward the $470–$480 area where it traded in late September.

stocks.name: American Express
stocks.move: Down about 2.9% shortly after the open Friday (9:41 a.m. ET, per TheStreet) after third-quarter results
stocks.why: American Express beat profit forecasts: adjusted earnings were $4.68 a share versus about $4.48 expected, and revenue rose 9% to $20.1 billion, roughly in line. It raised its 2026 adjusted profit forecast to $17.60–$17.90 a share and said it will cut about 5% of its global workforce. Shares still slipped because card spending volumes came in slightly below estimates, with total network volume of $517.9 billion against about $519.5 billion expected.
stocks.meaning: The results show wealthier card users are still spending, especially on travel, which is a decent sign for the consumer economy. But the stock often falls after good reports (Truist notes this would be its ninth drop in 11 quarters after a beat), so expectations were already high.

outlook.bullCase: If investors focus on the raised forecast and cost cuts, the stock could recover and test resistance near $327.
outlook.bearCase: Further worry about slowing spending growth or a weaker consumer, as oil prices squeeze budgets, could keep it under pressure.
outlook.watch: How it trades after the open, U.S. consumer sentiment at 10 a.m. today, and card-spending trends in other lenders' results.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.move: Down 0.7% to about $372 as of 3:23 p.m. ET, after touching $365 early; down 3.1% Thursday
stocks.why: Tesla rose during the day on Musk's comments that Tesla and SpaceX formed committees to study a merger. After the close it reported adjusted earnings of $0.48 a share versus about $0.45 expected and revenue of $28.05 billion, flat from a year ago and slightly below some forecasts; free cash flow of $1.5 billion beat expectations of a cash burn because spending came in about $3 billion lower than expected. Shares fell about 5% before the open as Tesla cut its 2026 capital-spending plan to about $20 billion from more than $25 billion and Musk said reaching 20,000 Optimus robots a week will take at least a year. Buyers erased the early loss after the open, but it slipped again as the Nasdaq weakened and closed near the day's low.
stocks.meaning: The core business is weak: operating income fell 56% to $718 million and deliveries slipped 2%, so the stock still trades mostly on robotaxi, Optimus and SpaceX-merger hopes. Lower spending helps cash flow but can read as a slower AI push, which explains the early selling.

outlook.bullCase: Concrete merger progress or a smooth Cybercab expansion to Dallas next month could bring it back toward $400–$410.
outlook.bearCase: If the early dip resumes and analysts trim targets, it could slide back toward $355–$375.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds the $365 area, merger committee news, and the NHTSA Cybercab response due Oct. 30.
